question: In the paper Attention Is All You Need, what positional encoding does the Transformer use? Answer in English.
answer: The Transformer uses fixed sinusoidal positional encodings built from sine and cosine functions of different frequencies, defined as PE(pos,2i) = sin(pos/10000^(2i/d_model)) and PE(pos,2i+1) = cos(pos/10000^(2i/d_model)), where pos is the position and i is the dimension (Corpus-Chunks800/artificial-intelligence__1706.03762__attention-is-all-you-need__k10.md). These encodings have the same dimension d_model as the embeddings so the two can be summed, and they are added to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks (Corpus-Chunks800/artificial-intelligence__1706.03762__attention-is-all-you-need__k09.md). The wavelengths form a geometric progression from 2π to 10000·2π, chosen because the authors hypothesized this would let the model easily learn to attend by relative positions, since PE(pos+k) can be represented as a linear function of PE(pos) (Corpus-Chunks800/artificial-intelligence__1706.03762__attention-is-all-you-need__k09.md). The paper notes it also tried learned positional embeddings and got nearly identical results, but chose the sinusoidal version for its potential to extrapolate to longer sequence lengths (Corpus-Chunks800/artificial-intelligence__1706.03762__attention-is-all-you-need__k09.md).
